answer.rationale: The competitor's price cut creates strong pressure to answer with promotional_pricing, but that is exactly the direction the record warns against: memory_73 records strong acquisition and revenue lift alongside a material 30-day retention drop and an explicit instruction not to generalize it. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching a price cut would likely buy short-term retention conversations while degrading the cohort quality that revenue depends on, and it would also anchor the SMB base to a discounted price point that is hard to unwind. The strongest evidence I hold that is both independently confirmed this cycle and retention-positive is exp_86 (shortened onboarding: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, 30-day retention +3%). Faster time-to-value is the most direct non-price defense against price-driven churn, because it raises perceived value before the renewal or switch decision. memory_31 (signup simplification) points the same way but is unverified, so I lean on memory_86 as the load-bearing evidence and treat memory_31 as corroborating rather than additive. exp_91 (activation messaging) is also confirmed and retention-positive but smaller on retention (+1%); I hold it as the next candidate rather than the lead, and it can be layered later without confounding the onboarding read. referral_incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not address the churning price-sensitive SMB segment; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment entirely and does not answer today's pressure. Key uncertainty I cannot resolve with the budget spent: exp_86's retention lift was measured on new self-serve accounts moving through onboarding, whereas the churn risk today sits in existing price-sensitive accounts that already completed onboarding. The mechanism may not transfer to that population. I therefore scope this as a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout, with instrumentation split between new signups and re-onboarding of at-risk existing accounts, so we learn whether the transfer holds instead of assuming it. If next cycle's budget reopens, memory_73 is the first re-verification priority, since any future pressure to discount should be decided against a fresh read of the retention damage, not an archived summary.
